messages.body_plain:
Rattle currently uses plotcorr() from ellipse. I am thinking to move to corrplot() from corrplot which includes a legend and arguably looks better. You can do the same by copying the code from the Rattle log tab into the R console to do the plotcorr(). Then

> install.packages("corrplot")
> library(corrplot)
> corrplot(crs$cor)

Similarly for any other plots generated by Rattle which do not do exactly what you want. Copy the code from the Rattle Log tab into the R Console to replicate the plot, then start fine tuning the code itself.

Graham Williams

messages.subject_clean: How to improve memory
messages.body_plain:
R is in-memory analytics. On 64 bit Windows with plenty of RAM you can load plenty more data.

On Ubuntu with 32GB RAM, for example, I can readily process 2 million observations by 1000 columns.

Extensive processing and model building may need 2 or 3 times that memory.

The more RAM the better, once you start talking about bigger datasets.

Graham Williams
http://togaware.com

On the Data tab, after loading a dataset, choose the Target Data Type as Survival. You can then choose the Time variable (time to event) and the Status variable (binary). Click Execute. Then on the Model tab Execute to build a Cox PH model. Some survival plots are then available. The Log tab shows the R commands if you need to do more, and ?coxph will provide further details.
